subject: Request: chain-of-custody, KMS logs, and Art.30 snapshot for DPIA archive
messages:
From: audit@cloudops.dev
To: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@novacorp.com
Date: 2027-06-09T08:52:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence request — DPIA archive / subprocessors handoff

Hi Jordan,

We're kicking off the DPIA archival review for NovaCorp and need to confirm a handful of items tied to the subprocessor transition that completed May 21. Specifically we need:

- A snapshot of the Article 30 processing register (CSV or Excel excerpt) that covers impacted processing activities between Jan 1 — May 31, 2027.
- Chain-of-custody evidence for data exports related to the migration (signed manifest + timestamps).
- KMS key rotation logs and the active key fingerprint(s) used for the exported archive.
- Confirmation of which subprocessors were involved in the export and whether any subprocessors performed decryption/transform steps.

Can you confirm turnaround and whether Redwood can provide a sampling approach (we prefer a 10% sample + attestation) rather than a full export? We also need the window for an auditor read-only access (SFTP or GDrive) and the name of the contact who can assist on technical access.

Attaching the audit intake form (see attachment stub). If you need to route to Legal / Security for redlines, please loop them in.

Thanks,

Alex Moran
CloudOps Audit
audit@cloudops.dev

Attachment: audit-intake-form.pdf (stub)

From: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
To: audit@cloudops.dev
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, legal@novacorp.com
Date: 2027-06-09T10:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — DPIA archive / subprocessors handoff

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We can support this request but want to confirm scope and practical constraints up front so we deliver precisely what the auditor needs without producing excessive exports. Proposed scope: 

1) Art.30 excerpt: a CSV export containing processing activity rows that map to NovaCorp's tenant id (tenant_nova_4387) for the Jan–May 2027 window. We will redact internal-only operational notes.
2) Chain-of-custody: signed manifest with MD5/SHA256 checksums for each exported bundle, plus timestamped transfer logs.
3) KMS proof: key fingerprint list + rotation audit (rotation events with timestamps and actor id). We cannot provide private key material, only rotation metadata and public fingerprints.
4) Subprocessor roles: a manifest listing subprocessors involved in export/transit and a short statement if any performed decryption/transform (yes/no + short description).

Sampling suggestion: provide a 10% sample of export bundles (randomized based on bundle id) with full chain-of-custody docs, plus an attestation letter from Redwood Security certifying the sampling method. If that is acceptable, we can avoid a full export.

Timeline: we can deliver the sample artifacts + Art.30 excerpt within 5 business days (target delivery: 2027-06-16). Full export would require an additional 7 business days and an internal change request.

Access: we'll provide a read-only Google Drive folder and SFTP fallback. Technical contact for access will be Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com).

I've attached an internal checklist and a short runbook for how we prepare the artifacts. If Legal needs to sign an audit access addendum, loop them in — Marissa will coordinate.

Next steps (please confirm):
- Approve sampling approach (10% sample + attestation)
- Confirm preferred access method (Drive or SFTP)
- Provide preferred delivery deadline (if earlier than 2027-06-16)

Regards,

Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: art30-processing-excerpt.xlsx (stub); chain_of_custody-snapshot.pdf (stub); dpiarunbook-v1.docx (stub)

From: audit@cloudops.dev
To: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@novacorp.com
Date: 2027-06-10T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — DPIA archive / subprocessors handoff

Thanks Jordan — that approach is acceptable. A few clarifications: 

- 10% sample is fine, but we need the randomization seed or method included in the attestation so our auditors can reproduce selection if required.
- For APAC subprocessors: NovaCorp's compliance team requests explicit confirmation whether any of the subprocessors in the manifest are located in Singapore or India and whether data was exported to those regions during the migration window.
- Please include the retention table mapping (data type -> retention period) from your Art.28 addendum for NovaCorp.
- Access method: Drive is preferred for initial delivery; SFTP will be used only if Drive transfer fails.

Auditor access window: we will perform a read-only review between 2027-06-17 and 2027-06-18. Please ensure the Drive folder is accessible by 2027-06-16 end of day.

Contact for the technical walkthrough: please confirm Karthik's mobile or an escalation contact (we sometimes need on-call access during snapshot review).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex Moran
CloudOps Audit

From: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
To: audit@cloudops.dev
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, legal@novacorp.com
Date: 2027-06-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — DPIA archive / subprocessors handoff

Alex —

Confirmed and summarized so there's no ambiguity: 

- Sampling: 10% randomized sample; attestation will include the random seed and the script/hash method (SHA256-based selection) so sampling can be reproduced.
- Art.30 excerpt: delivery as CSV (columns: activity_id, purpose, categories, recipient_types, legal_basis, storage_location, retention_period).
- Chain-of-custody: PDF manifest with checksums and signed transfer log entries.
- KMS: rotation event log CSV with key_fingerprint, rotation_timestamp, rotating_actor (system/service identity). No private key material provided.
- Subprocessors: manifest will mark APAC-located subprocessors; we will flag any export activity to Singapore/India explicitly.
- Retention table: included alongside the Art.30 excerpt.

Delivery plan: we will populate a read-only Drive folder by 2027-06-16 18:00 PDT and send an access link. Karthik will be on standby for the auditor walkthrough during the 2027-06-17 to 2027-06-18 window; mobile contact: +1-555-724-9911.

Marissa will upload the attestation letter (signed PDF) and the runbook excerpt that describes the sampling method. HubSpot record: DEAL-4387 has a support ticket (HS-2119) created for the artifact delivery — link below.

Drive link (will contain all artifacts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/requests/123456/HS-2119

If you need any additional evidence (forensics-level logs or a live session to run checks), escalate to Marissa and we'll coordinate the change request.

Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments to be uploaded: chain_of_custody-snapshot.pdf; kms-rotation-audit-202706.csv; art30-processing-excerpt.xlsx
